adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Indonesia - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's country overview supplies the national framework a visitor to East Java stands under, with no province-specific carve-out: Indonesian law provides no anti-discrimination or hate-crime protections based on sexual orientation or gender identity, and legal gender change requires sex-reassignment surgery plus a judge's approval. The 2022 penal-code amendment criminalising sex outside marriage - in force from 2 January 2026 - carries up to one year's imprisonment and effectively leaves same-sex couples with no recognised legal relationship of any kind. The page dates Indonesia's UN Human Rights Council votes against the independent expert on sexual orientation and gender identity in 2016, 2022 and 2025, records the Constitutional Court's 14 December 2017 5-4 ruling rejecting a petition to criminalise gay sex, and cites a 2025 Pew survey in which 93% of Indonesians call homosexuality 'morally unacceptable'. This corroborates the record's baseline that nothing in civil law constrains how East Java authorities handled the Isa Zega case - a trans woman was placed in a women's prison facility by identity with no anti-discrimination framework to contest it.

adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Indonesia - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's country overview grounds the record's at-national-score assessment for Bangka-Belitung Islands: no anti-discrimination or hate-crime protections exist for LGBT people, legal gender change requires sex-reassignment surgery plus judicial approval, and same-sex marriage, civil unions and domestic partnerships are unrecognised, so all same-sex sexual activity falls outside legal marriage. The 2022 penal-code amendment criminalising sex outside marriage, effective 2 January 2026, carries up to one year's imprisonment and applies to this division as to all of Indonesia. The page also records Indonesia's 2016, 2022 and 2025 votes against the UN independent expert on sexual orientation and gender identity, the Constitutional Court's 14 December 2017 5-4 rejection of a petition to criminalise gay sex, and a 2025 Pew figure of 93% of Indonesians rating homosexuality 'morally unacceptable' - the national baseline against which no Bangka-Belitung deviation has been documented.
